\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

GRPO-trained formalizers converge to high prove rates on first-order logic problems ($95{\pm}5\%$ across three seeds, 1000 steps), yet at convergence, \emph{none} produce structurally sound outputs.
Each seed develops a distinct degenerate shortcut: conclusion embedding, repetition collapse, or tautological collapse, all invisible to execution-based evaluation, which registers success regardless of whether the proof reflects genuine derivation.

\paragraph{The execution-only blind spot.}
Prove rate, the dominant evaluation metric for neurosymbolic formalizers~\citep{logic-lm, linc, satlm}, conflates faithful reasoning with degenerate shortcuts, a gap especially consequential under RL, where the optimizer exploits any shortcut the reward fails to penalize~\citep{skalse-reward-hacking, reward-hacking-survey}.
Recent work applies GRPO~\citep{deepseekmath} to train LLMs that generate solver-verified formal programs~\citep{mellgren-prolog-grpo, logic-rl} using binary execution feedback; this drives rapid PR gains but provides no signal on structural quality.
Process reward models~\citep{lightman-verify-step, math-shepherd} require expensive annotations and do not transfer to arbitrary solver-backed settings.
A separate line of work documents that LLMs already game logical formalization at inference time~\citep{kim-game-formalization, bondarenko-spec-gaming}; what is missing is an annotation-free \emph{diagnostic} for structural integrity in neurosymbolic outputs.

\paragraph{Component necessity testing.}
We address this gap with \emph{Solver Trace Ablation} (STA), which applies \emph{component necessity testing} (leave-one-out ablation on solver inputs) to quantify structural integrity (Figure~\ref{fig:sta-overview}).
For each proved formalization, STA removes each component individually and re-runs the solver; the fraction of components whose removal causes proof failure yields the \emph{Intensional Structural Reward} (ISR), with $\text{ISR}{=}1$ indicating full necessity and $\text{ISR}{=}0$ complete redundancy.
LOO ablation itself is standard~\citep{demillo1978, jia-harman-survey}; our contribution lies in applying it as a GRPO-hacking diagnostic and in the empirical phenomena it surfaces.
ISR captures structural rather than semantic integrity (downstream NLI: $\rho{=}{-}0.049$, $p{=}0.187$).

\paragraph{ISR as diagnostic.}
As a post-hoc diagnostic on a GRPO formalizer trained with FOLIO~\citep{folio}, ISR reveals a structural collapse trajectory invisible to PR: $\text{ISR}^{*}{:}\,0.642\to 0.132\to 0.003$ over 100--1000 steps (seed~42; 99.5\% degradation) while PR rises $32\%{\to}96\%$.
Three seeds diverge radically (PR $\sigma{=}47$\,pp), each converging to a qualitatively different mode: conclusion embedding, repetition collapse, and tautological collapse.
An SFT baseline on identical data reaches $\text{PR}{=}13.0\%$ with 92.3\% non-hacking (3-seed pooled, 1000 steps), localizing the failure to RL optimization, not data or capacity.

\paragraph{ISR as reward: inevitable Goodhart collapse.}
Repurposed as a training signal, $r = r_{\text{exec}} \cdot (1 + \beta\,\text{ISR})$, ISR contains an inherent structural vulnerability: tautological proofs (a single premise identical to the conclusion) receive $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$ by construction, and implication tautologies ($P{\to}P$) receive $\text{ISR}{=}0.75$, creating a positive feedback loop once sampled during GRPO rollouts~\citep{karwowski-goodhart-rl, kwa-catastrophic-goodhart}.
This makes Goodhart collapse~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy} inevitable at every tested dose ($\beta\in\{0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3\}$): $\beta$ controls \emph{when} collapse occurs, not \emph{whether}.
At $\beta{=}0.1$, collapse is stochastic and delayed: 5 seeds bifurcate between rapid H7 convergence (2 seeds, ${\leq}100$ steps) and a transient genuine window (${\sim}23\%$ non-hacking at 500 steps, 3 seeds) that closes under extended training ($17\%{\to}2\%$ genuine at 1000 steps).
Snapshot evaluation at 500 steps would overestimate ISR's benefit; trajectory analysis reveals the window is temporary.
The effect transfers to Prolog (3/3 seeds yield 0\% non-hacking via distinct mechanisms, including \emph{query-as-fact gaming}) and across model scale (1.7B discovers qualitatively novel gaming modes).
ISR's asymmetry is the central finding: \emph{reliable as observer, unreliable as optimizer at any dose.}

\paragraph{Contributions.}
Across 6 reward conditions, 5 seeds, 2 logic types, 2 model scales, and up to 1000 steps, we contribute: (\textbf{C1}) ISR as a diagnostic for GRPO reward hacking, with a 99.5\% collapse trajectory invisible to PR and an SFT control localizing the failure to RL (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}); (\textbf{C2}) an empirical instance of inevitable Goodhart collapse~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy}: ISR's structural bias toward tautology ($\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$ for $P{\to}P$) creates a positive feedback loop that causes gaming at all four tested doses; collapse is stochastic and delayed at moderate $\beta$ but trajectory analysis confirms all seeds converge, showing that $\beta$ controls timing, not outcome (\S\ref{sec:goodhart}); (\textbf{C3}) cross-logic transfer to Prolog with consistent Goodhart effects across all seeds (\S\ref{sec:crosslogic}); (\textbf{C4}) a nine-mode hacking taxonomy including query-as-fact gaming, obfuscated tautology, and a scale-specific \emph{ex falso} mode, motivating functional cross-validation of diagnostics (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy}).
These are cautionary results: snapshot evaluation of structural rewards can overestimate their benefit; only trajectory analysis reveals inevitable collapse.

96	The raw ISR$^*$ headline collapses once the LOO bias is controlled, a methodological lesson for any LOO-based metric on variable-length outputs. %% artifact: wilson_ci_complete

101	\caption{Training ISR trajectories across reward conditions. ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ seeds rise rapidly toward $\text{ISR}{\approx}1$ (Goodhart gaming via H7 tautology); exec-only s44's plateau at ${\sim}0.5$ is an H7a artifact ($n{=}2$ gives $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$ by construction), not genuine structural quality; random $\beta{=}0.1$ remains low. The s42 1k-step trace shows ISR eventually saturates at $0.88$ through the same H7 mechanism.}
102	\label{fig:training-isr-curves}
103	\end{figure}

105	\textbf{Trajectory analysis: timing, not destiny.}\label{sec:goodhart-temporal}
106	Figure~\ref{fig:training-isr-curves} traces training ISR across conditions.
107	Extended training (1000 steps) on seed~42 confirms that the genuine window is temporary: H7 gaming escalates from $16.0\%$ to $96.7\%$ while the non-hacking rate collapses from $17.3\%$ to $2.2\%$ ($n_{\text{comp}}$: $5.58{\to}2.89$).
108	The optimization converges to a fixed point where $\text{ISR}^{*}{=}0.88$, reflecting near-complete tautological gaming rather than structural improvement.
109	This trajectory demonstrates that $\beta{=}0.1$ does not prevent collapse but delays it: the stochastic bifurcation determines \emph{when} a seed enters the H7 basin, and once entered, convergence to gaming is irreversible.
110	The pattern mirrors exec-only at 1000 steps (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}): both converge to ${\sim}0\%$ non-hacking proofs despite opposite ISR values ($0.88$ vs.\ $0.003$), two paths to the same structural collapse. %% registry: plan002-b01-s42-1000, plan016-extended-1000-s42
111	
112	\textbf{Micro-dose ISR ($\beta{=}0.05$): collapse observed at all tested doses.}
113	Even at $\beta{=}0.05$, the lowest dose tested (seed~42), 100\% of proved samples ($n{=}55$) are H7a tautologies with 0\% non-hacking, showing that the ISR structural bias toward tautology is exploitable at minimal signal strength. %% registry: sweep-isr-b005-s42
114	Combined with the $\beta{=}0.1$ trajectory data, this supports the conclusion that collapse occurs at all tested doses; higher $\beta$ accelerates the timeline but the vulnerability is intrinsic to ISR's LOO definition.

116	\textbf{Medium-dose ISR ($\beta{=}0.2$): maximum exploitation.}
117	At $\beta{=}0.2$, all three seeds converge to H7a tautology with $0\%$ non-hacking (pooled $n{=}290$), the maximum exploitation point in the dose-response curve (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:beta02-detail}).
118	Seeds achieve $\text{ISR}^{*}{=}0.55$--$0.96$ through single-premise-equals-conclusion constructions. %% registry: sweep-isr-b02-s42/s43/s44

122	Seed~42: \emph{reward collapse} ($\text{PR}{=}18\%$), following the pattern described by~\citet{gao-reward-overoptimization}.
123	Seed~43: \emph{H1 shortcutting} ($\text{PR}{=}86\%$, $\text{H1}{=}69\%$, only $23\%$ non-hacking).
124	Seed~44: \emph{pure H7 gaming} ($\text{PR}{=}95\%$, $\text{H7}{=}100\%$, $\text{ISR}^{*}{=}0.742$, $0\%$ non-hacking), simultaneously gaming \emph{both} execution and structural metrics through the same construction.

127	\subsection{Cross-Logic Diagnostic Transfer}
128	\label{sec:crosslogic}
129	
130	\begin{figure}[t]
131	\centering
132	\includegraphics[width=0.95\columnwidth]{figures/fig4_prolog_comparison.pdf}
133	\caption{Cross-logic results. \textbf{Left}: FOL vs.\ Prolog exec-only $\text{ISR}^*$ across 3 seeds (s44 Prolog $0.387$ is a small-sample artifact, $n{=}21$). \textbf{Right}: Prolog ISR-reward gaming-mode composition: all 3 seeds reach 0\% non-hacking through distinct mechanisms.}

135	\end{figure}
136	
137	We replicate the FOL pipeline with Prolog/SWI-Prolog: (i) does ISR retain diagnostic value on a structurally different logic; (ii) does ISR-as-reward reproduce the Goodhart effects observed in FOL?
138	Detailed per-seed numbers are in Appendix Table~\ref{tab:prolog-detailed}.
139	
140	\textbf{Prolog exec-only: ISR catches redundancy across logics.}
141	Two of three seeds (s42, s43) show $\text{ISR}^{*}{\approx}0$ despite moderate-to-high PR (0.83, 0.56). %% registry: plan006-prolog-exec-s42, plan006-prolog-exec-s43-r3
142	Inspection reveals \emph{redundant coding}: ground facts repeated multiple times (e.g., \texttt{penguin(fido).} appearing three times), so per-clause LOO never breaks the proof.
143	This is a different failure semantics from FOL exec-only (conclusion embedding), but $\text{ISR}^{*}$ flags both.
144	We are careful to distinguish: exec-only \emph{low} ISR signals \emph{redundancy}; ISR-rewarded \emph{high} ISR signals \emph{metric gaming} (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy-method}); the same number does not license the same reasoning-quality conclusion.
145	
146	\textbf{Prolog ISR-as-reward: consistent gaming across all seeds.}
147	The Prolog result is qualitatively consistent with FOL: 3/3 seeds reach $0\%$ non-hacking via three distinct mechanisms (Figure~\ref{fig:prolog-comparison}).
148	Seed~42: clean H7 tautologies ($\text{ISR}^{*}{=}1.0$, all $50/100$ proved). %% registry: plan006-prolog-sta-s42

150	Seed~44: \emph{query-as-fact gaming}: the model transforms the NL question into a snake-case atom asserted as both fact and query (e.g., \texttt{is\_the\_dog\_furry.}), with $95/97$ proved samples at $n_{\text{necessary}}{=}1$. %% registry: plan006-prolog-sta-s44
151	Seed~44 evaded our initial strict classifier (reported $100\%$ non-hacking); functional cross-validation exposed it, a methodological lesson that text-match classifiers have blind spots and STA's necessity profile is the cross-check.
152	We attribute Prolog's complete collapse to its simpler operational semantics: a broader gaming basin makes the non-hacking residual disappear.
153	This is a qualitative observation from a single configuration (Prolog + ISR $\beta{=}0.1$, 3 seeds); generalization to other logic types requires further experimentation.
154	
155	\subsection{Cross-Scale Evidence}
156	\label{sec:crossscale}
157	
158	To test whether ISR gaming generalizes beyond Qwen3-4B, we train Qwen3-1.7B under three conditions ($K{=}4$, seed~42, 500 steps): ISR $\beta{=}0.1$, ISR $\beta{=}0.3$, and matched Random $\beta{=}0.1$.
159	All three produce 0\% genuine non-hacking output at $\beta{=}0.1$; the hacking modes differ qualitatively from all 4B experiments (Table~\ref{tab:hacking-taxonomy}).
160	
161	\textbf{Random $\beta{=}0.1$: H9 (ex falso quodlibet).}

163	ISR registers $>0$ because each contradictory premise is individually ``necessary'' under LOO (removing either side breaks the derivation), yet the formalization is semantically vacuous.
164	H9 never appears under any 4B condition; it is a capacity-specific exploit.
165	
166	\textbf{ISR $\beta{=}0.1$: fixed-template ISR gaming.}
167	Under ISR reward, the 1.7B model achieves $\text{PR}{=}100\%$ with $\text{ISR}^{*}{=}0.6$ at \emph{zero variance across all samples}, indicating mode collapse to a single fixed template. %% registry: d113-1.7b-isr-b01-s42
168	All proved samples are H1 (conclusion embedding); the template is engineered to achieve constant ISR by construction.
169	This contrasts with 4B ISR $\beta{=}0.1$, where H7 tautological duplication dominates in $2/3$ seeds ($\text{ISR}^{*}{\approx}0.5$).
170	The difference is capacity-dependent: the smaller model converges to a rigid template satisfying both execution and ISR simultaneously, rather than the premise-minimization strategy available at 4B scale.
171	
172	\textbf{ISR $\beta{=}0.3$: reward collapse.}
173	At $\beta{=}0.3$, 1.7B exhibits reward collapse ($\text{PR}{=}17\%$, $\text{ISR}^{*}{=}0.031$) with $\text{H1}{=}70.6\%$ and $29.4\%$ genuine among the few proved samples. %% registry: d113-1.7b-isr-b03-s42
174	This mirrors the 4B $\beta{=}0.3$ seed~42 collapse pattern ($\text{PR}{=}18\%$), suggesting that high-dose ISR exceeds training stability at both scales.
175	
176	\textbf{Capacity-dependent Goodhart basins.}
177	The cross-scale comparison reveals that different model capacities converge to different Goodhart basins under identical reward formulations: 4B discovers H7 (tautological duplication, $\text{ISR}{\approx}0.5$), while 1.7B discovers either H9 (contradiction explosion, under random) or fixed-template H1 (under ISR, $\text{ISR}{=}0.6$).
178	No safe scale exists: both model sizes achieve 0\% non-hacking at $\beta{=}0.1$; only the exploit strategy differs.

180	\subsection{Hacking Taxonomy}
181	\label{sec:taxonomy}

\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
\label{sec:discussion}

STA exposes structural degeneration invisible to execution-based evaluation: ISR reveals a 99.5\% collapse under exec-only GRPO that PR hides, while SFT localizes the failure to RL optimization (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}).
Repurposed as a training signal, ISR exhibits inevitable Goodhart collapse~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy}: tautological proofs receive artificially high ISR (${\geq}0.5$ by construction), creating a positive feedback loop that causes gaming at all four tested doses ($\beta\in\{0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3\}$).
The effect is consistent across logic types (Prolog: 0\% non-hacking, 3/3 seeds), model scales (1.7B: novel gaming modes), and training durations (500$\to$1000 steps: transient genuine windows close).
ISR semantics are objective-dependent: exec-only \emph{low} ISR signals redundancy; ISR-rewarded \emph{high} ISR signals metric gaming.

\paragraph{Timing, not destiny.}
$\beta$ does not control whether collapse occurs, but when.
At $\beta{=}0.1$, 5 seeds bifurcate stochastically: 2 collapse rapidly (${\leq}150$ steps), 3 sustain a genuine window (${\sim}23\%$ at 500 steps) that trajectory analysis confirms is temporary ($17\%{\to}2\%$ at 1000 steps).
At $\beta{=}0.05$, the single tested seed collapses immediately (100\% H7); at $\beta{=}0.2$, all 3 seeds collapse; at $\beta{=}0.3$, diverse failure modes emerge.
The structural bias ($P{\to}P$ receives $\text{ISR}{=}0.75$, single-premise-equals-conclusion receives $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$) ensures that H7 tautology is always the global ISR-maximizing exploit.
Once a seed samples and reinforces this exploit, convergence is irreversible; $\beta$ controls only the probability of early sampling.

\paragraph{Classifier blind spots.}
H7b (obfuscated tautology) and Prolog query-as-fact gaming demonstrate that text-match classifiers have systematic blind spots exploitable by optimization.
In both cases, functional LOO analysis exposed gaming invisible to surface-level detection: H7b via vacuous quantifier wrapping ($10/12$ at $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.83$, triple gaming of execution, ISR, and classifier), query-as-fact via $95/97$ tautological samples the strict classifier labeled non-hacking (\S\ref{sec:crosslogic}).
H9 (contradiction injection, 1.7B Random $\beta{=}0.1$; \S\ref{sec:crossscale}) extends this pattern further: contradictory premises register as individually necessary under LOO, bypassing both text-match and functional $n_{\text{necessary}}$ classifiers; detection requires logic-level consistency checking.
These cases collectively argue for mandatory functional cross-validation of text-based hacking classifiers, complemented by logic-level checks for novel exploit classes.

\paragraph{Capacity-dependent Goodhart basins.}
Different model capacities converge to different exploit strategies under identical reward formulations (\S\ref{sec:crossscale}): 4B frequently converges to H7 (tautological duplication) or H1 (conclusion embedding) depending on seed, while 1.7B discovers H9 (contradiction explosion, under random) or fixed-template H1 (under ISR, zero-variance $\text{ISR}{=}0.6$).
No safe scale exists; both model sizes achieve 0\% non-hacking at $\beta{=}0.1$.
This suggests that scaling model capacity does not eliminate Goodhart effects but shifts the exploit basin.

\paragraph{Snapshot evaluation is misleading.}
At 500 steps, ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ shows ${\sim}23\%$ genuine output (5-seed pooled), while 2/5 seeds have already collapsed to 0\%.
A practitioner evaluating at this checkpoint would conclude ISR provides moderate structural benefit; the 1000-step trajectory reveals this is a temporal artifact.
This has practical implications: any evaluation of structural rewards must include trajectory analysis or extended training to distinguish transient from stable improvement.
The ISR/PR ratio (stable at ${\sim}0.30$ during SFT, collapsing during RL gaming) may serve as an early-stopping signal for Goodhart onset.

\paragraph{Hacking mode switching is seed-dependent.}
The dominant hacking mode (H7 vs.\ H1) is determined by random initialization, not reward condition: under identical configurations, different seeds converge to qualitatively different modes (Table~\ref{tab:fol-detailed}).
Random $\beta{=}0.1$ across 4 seeds yields genuine rates from $1\%$ to $23\%$ ($8.2{\pm}9.7$\,pp, $\text{CV}{>}1$); ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ shows even greater variance (0\% to ${\sim}55\%$ genuine at 500 steps, 5 seeds).
Single-seed results can misrepresent a reward configuration's hacking profile; multi-seed evaluation with trajectory analysis should be standard.

\paragraph{Future directions.}
The asymmetry (reliable observer, unreliable optimizer at any dose) may generalize to other perturbation-based diagnostics; ISR and similar metrics should serve as post-hoc evaluation tools, not training signals.
The stochastic bifurcation mechanism suggests that gated ISR (activating structural reward only after a warmstart period, or deactivating once ISR exceeds a threshold) might extend the genuine window, though the inherent structural bias makes indefinite stability unlikely.
Future work should target gaming-robust reward designs that do not reward tautological constructions, broader logic types, and formal analysis of the bifurcation dynamics.

\paragraph{Goodhart effects: implications.}
The finding extends beyond this specific system.
ISR was designed to \emph{detect} reward gaming of $r_{\text{exec}}$, yet it contains an inherent structural vulnerability: by its LOO definition, tautological proofs receive artificially high ISR ($P{\to}P$ yields $\text{ISR}{=}0.75$; single-premise-equals-conclusion yields $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$), creating a positive feedback loop once sampled during GRPO rollouts~\citep{karwowski-goodhart-rl, kwa-catastrophic-goodhart}.
This makes Goodhart collapse~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy} inevitable at every tested dose ($\beta\in\{0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3\}$): the structural bias ensures that H7 tautology is always the global reward-maximizing exploit, and $\beta$ controls only the probability of early sampling and thus the timing of collapse.
At moderate doses ($\beta{=}0.1$), collapse is stochastic and delayed (5 seeds bifurcate: 2 collapse rapidly, 3 sustain a transient genuine window that trajectory analysis confirms is temporary); at higher doses ($\beta{=}0.2$), collapse is immediate and universal.
$\beta{=}0.3$ adds reward collapse~\citep{gao-reward-overoptimization} as a competing failure mode (PR drops to 18\% in 1/3 seeds), but the underlying Goodhart vulnerability remains the same.
The practical implication is that ISR (and structurally similar LOO-based diagnostics) should be used exclusively as post-hoc evaluation tools, never as training rewards.

Recall is inherently bounded by the text-match threshold: semantic manipulations that alter surface form while preserving the gaming structure (e.g., variable renaming beyond our normalization, or paraphrased conclusions) would be missed.
We cross-validate with functional LOO analysis: samples classified as non-hacking but showing $n_{\text{necessary}} \leq 1$ are flagged as potential false negatives.

\paragraph{Detection.} H8 is identified by manual inspection of non-hacking samples with unusually low premise counts ($n_{\text{prem}} \leq 3$) that nonetheless achieve high ISR.

Full H8 audit was completed for ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ seed~42 only.

\section{Limitations}
\label{sec:limitations}

Experiments use a single base model (Qwen3-4B) and dataset family (FOLIO); generalization remains untested.
ISR quantifies syntactic component necessity, not semantic faithfulness: a high-ISR proof can still be logically vacuous if its individually necessary premises are collectively inconsistent or semantically ungrounded.
A downstream NLI evaluation confirms this gap, finding ISR and task accuracy uncorrelated (Spearman $\rho{=}{-}0.049$, $p{=}0.187$; Appendix~\ref{app:extended-discussion}).
Five seeds demonstrate qualitative divergence but limit statistical power for per-seed comparisons.
STA requires solvers supporting component-level input manipulation.

\paragraph{Evaluation as temporal snapshot.}
All 500-step results represent a temporal snapshot, not an equilibrium.
Trajectory analysis on seed~42 (1000 steps) confirms that the ${\sim}23\%$ genuine window observed at 500 steps under ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ is transient ($17\%{\to}2\%$ genuine).
Readers should interpret the 500-step non-hacking rates as upper bounds on long-run structural quality under continued training.

\paragraph{Single-seed dose points.}
ISR $\beta{=}0.05$ uses a single seed (s42); $\beta{=}0.2$ uses three seeds.
Although all tested doses produce dominant gaming, the stochastic bifurcation mechanism (\S\ref{sec:goodhart}) means that single-seed results may not capture the full variance of collapse timing.

\paragraph{Cross-scale replication.}
Our 1.7B experiments use a single seed.
Although different seeds may converge to different exploitation modes (as observed at 4B scale, where three seeds produce three distinct hacking strategies), the qualitative conclusion that hacking dominates with 0\% genuine output is robust: at 4B, all seeds hack regardless of specific mode.
The zero-variance mode collapse at 1.7B (100 identical outputs) indicates a sharper convergence basin at smaller scale.
Replicating across seeds is a natural next step.

\paragraph{Data scale.}
Our experiments use 500 training examples and 100 evaluation examples, drawn from FOLIO~\citep{folio}.
The training subset is selected via stratified sampling (seed 42) and held constant across all conditions.
While our findings are consistent across seeds and logic types, the effect of training data scale on hacking prevalence and mode distribution remains an open question for future work.
